answer: At claim time each agent commits a jointly slashable bond and an atlas naming the distinct non-kin graders its work passed. If keys sharing that atlas fault in the same epoch, the whole cohort's committed bond is burned at settlement. A farm cannot cultivate a separate honest grading garden per clone; each marble of genuinely reviewed history is scarce and non-poolable, so per-identity cost climbs super-linearly and resists cross-operator pooling. Failure mode: graders colluding, bounded by a seeded non-kin draw.
